We then study incentives that reward correct independent work and characterize the payments needed to encourage skill acquisition and retention. We show that independent work can become self-sustaining once workers acquire sufficient skill, eliminating the need for continued incentives. Counterintuitively, supporting a higher skill target can sometimes reduce long-run incentive costs, either by enabling self-sustaining independent work or by lowering the payments needed to maintain proficiency. Our findings thereby shift the focus from whether workers should rely on AI on individual tasks to how organizations can sustain human expertise over time, and which skills are worth investing in.
papers.comment: 30 pages, 6 figures, 6 tables. Moritz Diener and Daniel Hendriks contributed equally

papers.title: CoRTeC: A Differentially Private Release for Synthetic Tabular Data, Decodable by Any Generator
papers.summary: The records that could train the most useful models, such as a hospital's patient files, are often the ones an institution cannot share. We propose CoRTeC, a method that releases synthetic versions of such records under differential privacy. Differential privacy places a proven limit on what the synthetic data can reveal about any person, and in particular on membership inference. CoRTeC spends the privacy budget once, on a small file of noisy counts designed for training a classifier. For each group of records, the file gives the group's size, its balance of outcomes, a histogram of every column for each outcome and the outcome rate in each of several non-overlapping cells. A reviewer can check every number before the file leaves the institution. Anyone can then turn the counts into synthetic rows, as often as they like and at no further privacy cost. A maximum-entropy decoder can do this without any language model, and so can each of the five frozen language models we tested. None of them ever sees a real record. A selection step then matches the rows to the released counts. Decoded without a language model, the automatically configured release at $\varepsilon = 2$ trains classifiers to within 0.02 AUC of a real sample of the same size on the Adult dataset, across three data splits. On NHANES and bank marketing, without the selection step, it stays within 0.05 AUC. On Adult, with a fixed cohort rule, the release carries the outcome rates a deployment names more closely than a real sample does, at some cost in accuracy on pairs of columns. Four controls show that most of the utility comes from the release and the selection step, and that a language model adds what it knows from the column names. No private row ever reaches a model, and no row CoRTeC generates copies a real one. The strongest membership attack stays far below the bound the budget allows.
papers.comment: 29 pages, 4 figures. Code at https://github.com/Calyie/cortec and the releases, synthetic draws and score files at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22945315

papers.title: Primordial Black Holes and Induced Gravitational Waves from Inflation with History-Dependent Effective Dissipation
papers.summary: We study inflation with an exponential factor multiplying the scalar Lagrangian and depending on the accumulated expansion history through a field-dependent coupling. Variation of the complete action on a finite interval yields an adjoint response with a final-time boundary condition. We derive the background and coupled scalar perturbation equations and examine five benchmarks for an exponential plateau potential and a smooth single-window coupling. The kinetic, direct-coupling and adjoint contributions nearly cancel, producing transient positive minima of the first Hubble slow-roll parameter, $ε_1$, without a comparable reduction in field velocity. The scalar spectra, normalized to the cosmic microwave background (CMB) pivot amplitude, develop localized peaks with amplitudes $0.033$--$0.098$. Under Gaussian statistics and the adopted radiation-era collapse prescription, the the primordial black hole (PBH) abundance peaks span masses from $4.52\times10^{-13}$ to $34.05\,M_\odot$. The lightest-mass benchmark reaches $f_{\rm PBH}\simeq0.99$, allowing nearly all dark matter within the monochromatic approximation. The accompanying scalar-induced gravitational-wave spectra span peak frequencies from $6.78\times10^{-10}$ to $5.92\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{Hz}$, with selected benchmarks lying within the projected sensitivities of future detectors.

papers.title: A plea for Miles' approach to wind-wave interaction
papers.summary: Although the phenomenon of wave growth under the effect of wind still holds many open questions, the approach initiated by Miles [1] is a cornerstone of the current comprehension. This theory is based on physical arguments, keeping phenomenological input to a minimum, but it can be perceived as intimidating, especially in view of concrete applications. Here we argue that Miles' results can be summarised in terms of a simple functional form, which provides an easy-to-use expression to work with. We furthermore show that Miles' predictions do not, as is often stated, underestimate growth rates, once the presence of a whole wave spectrum is accounted for. Finally, we illustrate that the generalisation of Miles' original result to complex hydrodynamic situations can be quite straightforward. Our hands-on summary should make it heretofore very easy to exploit Miles' approach in practice.

papers.title: Scale Anchoring via Implicit Semantics and Sequence-Consistent Loop Closure for VGGT-Based SLAM
papers.summary: Feed-forward geometric foundation models enable dense monocular reconstruction without requiring camera calibration, but independently reconstructed submaps can accumulate scale drift, and even a valid revisit can yield an inconsistent cross-submap measurement. We extend VGGT-SLAM 2.0 with fixed-root scale anchoring and short-sequence-assisted direct loop connections. SALAD selects an image pair between the initial submap and each eligible new submap; joint VGGT inference then uses learned implicit semantic-geometric cues to supply a scale-only anchor while preserving the original overlap chain. For loop closure, neighboring image pairs support a consistency check and translation-scale alignment. Each accepted candidate contributes one robust Sim(3) factor between existing center-frame nodes, without an auxiliary loop submap. A 17-sequence comparison lowers mean Sim(3) ATE on nine TUM sequences from 0.1018 to 0.0451 m relative to the VGGT-SLAM 2.0 baseline. Anchoring improves all seven no-loop module ablations. On three Clio scenes, a fixed-loop comparison favors the direct connection pipeline over the tested auxiliary-submap pipeline. A separate candidate audit exposes additional rejections of visually overlapping pairs by the short-sequence check. These comparisons distinguish the gains from long-range scale anchoring and loop connection choices from the limitations of candidate verification.
papers.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to IEEE ICRA 2027

papers.title: Spectral flow in AdS$\mathbf{_3}$ revisited
papers.summary: We revisit an old idea that spectral flow in WZW models can be associated with certain $G$-bundles over a worldsheet. This allows us to introduce a novel method for computing correlators of spectrally-flowed vertex operators in WZW models with group $G$ and level $k$, by systematically computing the contribution from a network of line defects. Specialising to the case of $G=SL(2, \mathbb{R})$, as is relevant to AdS$_3$ string theory, we demonstrate that generic $n$-point functions of spectrally-flowed vertex operators at tree level can be rewritten in terms of an $(n+1)$-point function of $n$ unflowed vertex operators and one degenerate insertion. This is to be interpreted as an unflowed $n$-point function in an instanton background. Moreover, we conjecture that this $(n+1)$-point function can be recast as an $n$-point function of unflowed operators and we provide evidence for this. We demonstrate that the $(n+1)$-point function satisfies the same constraints from global spacetime conformal invariance as does an unflowed $n$-point function for a specific choice of spacetime coordinates that we determine. We verify that our results agree with bootstrap results in the literature. This provides the next step towards fully solving the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ WZW model.
papers.comment: 66 pages, 6 figures. Includes ancillary Mathematica notebook

papers.title: A.S.E 2.0: Understanding How Repository Context Impacts the Security of LLM-Generated Code
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) coding assistants and agents construct a repository context before generating code. For security-sensitive code, this context decides whether the model sees the project's safeguards (e.g., authorization checks) or insecure code to imitate. However, context construction is designed almost exclusively for functional correctness, and secure-code benchmarks treat the context as fixed, so how repository context affects the security of generated code remains unclear. We construct CASE-Bench, a benchmark of 145 repository-level tasks from real CVEs in 51 projects. Each task runs in Docker, has functional tests and a proof-of-concept exploit validated in both directions, and is annotated with the repository code that enforces or undermines its security. Using CASE-Bench, we compare 13 context construction methods and six controls with six LLMs, edit single context elements, and analyze coding-agent trajectories. We find that (1) functionality-oriented context raises the functional pass rate by up to 8.2 percentage points (pp) but the secure pass rate by at most 3.7 pp, (2) withholding a safeguard lowers the secure pass rate by up to 8.1 pp, while one inserted insecure exemplar raises correct-but-exploitable code by 6.3 pp, and (3) coding agents observe the relevant safeguard in only 27-36% of trajectories. These findings inform security-aware context construction and secure-code evaluation.

papers.title: Corridor-Based Monitoring and Emergency Braking Decision for Automated Vehicle Safety
papers.summary: This paper addresses emergency-braking decisions for a redundant safety channel in automated vehicles. The channel is responsible for identifying hazards from sensor data and determining whether braking is necessary, given the constrained computational resources of embedded hardware. We present an emergency-braking approach that uses a predicted motion corridor to filter \ac{lidar} measurements and then decide whether the ego vehicle must brake. \ac{pmcm} constructs a curvature-aware boundary from the planned path and vehicle geometry so that the monitored region contains the full swept body on both straight and curved paths. \ac{gdeta} then decides whether the ego vehicle must command an emergency brake for objects inside this boundary, scoring geometric occupancy and temporal urgency independently. Hard gates permit braking when either source is conclusive; soft-OR arbitration combines partial evidence when neither gate is active. Consecutive-scan confirmation reduces sensitivity to transient measurement noise. Corridor coverage is evaluated in controlled collision simulations and recorded campus driving. Braking decisions are evaluated in Monte Carlo simulations of lead-vehicle braking and transverse-crossing encounters.
papers.comment: Submitted to a Springer Nature journal for peer review as an extended version of a paper presented at VEHITS, for consideration in the Special Issue

papers.title: Clear Human Web: Where a Person Vouches for Every Client
papers.summary: The web cannot tell whether a request comes from a person or from a program. Sites have checked the network address and puzzles in its place, and both have given way: automated traffic exceeds human traffic, and puzzles are solved for pay and by agents. This paper proposes the Clear Human Web, the part of the public web that sites open only to clients a person vouches for. A person's wallet presents their person identification data (PID) to one issuer, the only party that registers as a relying party, and receives a bounded number of blind-signed tokens, proofs of personhood that carry no attribute. The browser spends one token at each site that runs the gate, and the site learns that a valid token of a trusted issuer was spent, and nothing else. No field is added to the PID, no protocol is introduced, no site registers, and the publisher of a site holds the same proof as its readers. We define the Clear Human Web through five properties and seven adversaries, and state which properties the construction satisfies against each adversary. The identities a person can hold on one site in an epoch are bounded to k. The bound holds once the wallet limits a person to one pseudonym at the issuer. In the optimum k = 1, and a zero-knowledge proof of PID possession and a pseudonym per site replace the tokens.

papers.title: A search for sterile neutrinos at ultrahigh energies at the Pierre Auger Observatory
papers.summary: We investigate the sensitivity of the Pierre Auger Observatory to sterile neutrinos with masses in the MeV-to-100 MeV range. To this end, we consider a minimal $3+1$ framework in which a single sterile state mixes mainly with the $ν_τ$ flavor through an active--sterile mixing angle $θ_N$ to produce a mass eigenstate $N_1$. At ultrahigh energies, $N_1$ neutrinos can traverse substantial chord lengths through the Earth and interact through their active component, producing $τ$ leptons that may emerge near the surface and decay in the atmosphere, thereby generating detectable air showers. We compute the corresponding exposures with a detailed Monte Carlo simulation of neutrino propagation, interactions, $τ$ energy losses and decay, and derive upper limits at $90\%$ confidence level on an isotropic diffuse flux of $N_1$ neutrinos. For an $E^{-2}$ spectrum, we obtain $E^2Φ_N\leq 2\times10^{-9}\sin^{-2}θ_N\,\mathrm{GeV\,cm^{-2}\,sr^{-1}\,s^{-1}}$ over $0.3$--$200$ EeV for $\sin^2θ_N\lesssim10^{-1}$. We further consider $N_1$ neutrinos arising from the decay of a superheavy dark-matter particle. For a benchmark dark-matter mass of $10^{13}$ GeV, we derive constraints on the active--sterile mixing angle and dark-matter lifetime for sterile-neutrino masses of $10$ and $100$ MeV. These results illustrate the potential of the Observatory to probe long-lived weakly interacting particles.
authors: J. R. T. de Mello Neto

papers.title: All reweighted paths lead to Rome: Unification of reweighting schemes for stratified path sampling
papers.summary: Path sampling-based stratification algorithms such as Transition Interface Sampling (TIS) enable the evaluation of kinetic rate constants and mechanisms of complex molecular rare event transitions. By sampling only short dynamical trajectories, TIS allows constructing an estimate of the unbiased dynamics by reweighting the interface path ensembles. In the past decades several methods have been developed and applied to achieve such path reweighting, based on statistically optimal use of the trajectory data. Why and how this reweighting exactly works has been underexplored up to now. Here we discuss several different schemes to compute the reweighted path ensemble (RPE), notably point-wise matching, Weighted Histogram Analysis Method (WHAM), Multistate Bennett Acceptance Ratio (MBAR), variance based reweighting (VBR) and survival analysis reweighting (SAR). We show that except for the point-wise matching the other methods are leading to the same outcome, and in fact can be seen as identical. Moreover, the SAR links to a well-established nonparametric maximum-likelihood estimator of product-limit form. This allows a synthesis of all path reweighting schemes, identifying the common underlying nature. All schemes follow from this common origin. We illustrate the reweighting with some simple examples, and show that care has to be taken when applying WHAM, if the number of interfaces and histogram bins do not match.

papers.title: A Design Rule for Passive Reconfigurable Microwave Devices
papers.summary: Every reconfigurable microwave device places a tuning element - a varactor, a diode, transistor, microelectromechanical or phase-change switch, a ferroelectric or liquid-crystal load - inside a fixed passive network. The network can make a small change of the element produce a large change of the response, and design practice often credits it with the device's tuning capability. This paper shows that a fixed, linear, passive network cannot add to that capability. Each tuning element carries a tuning budget, a dimensionless length computed from its own impedance trajectory, and a fixed passive network can transmit that budget or lose part of it, never enlarge it. The unit of the budget is the hyperbolic distance of the Smith chart: the distance from a match is the logarithm of the voltage standing-wave ratio, and the distance between two states sets their mutual mismatch and is the logarithm of their commutation quality factor. From one inequality we derive closed-form, ready-to-use limits for analog and digital phase shifters, true-time-delay lines, switches, attenuators, vector modulators, impedance tuners, tunable filters, reconfigurable antennas, metasurface cells and multiport networks; the two-state and attenuation limits are attained by explicit circuits, and the phase limit by a constant-loss trajectory. We introduce the $Λ$-chart, a Smith-chart companion on which budgets and requirements are read graphically, and apply it to four published microwave case studies.
papers.comment: 42 pages total (11 pages main manuscript, 31 pages supplementary information); 9 figures

papers.title: Evaluating Human-LLM Alignment on Visualization Preference
papers.summary: There are often multiple valid visualizations, spanning different chart types, visual encodings, and aesthetic choices, that can all support a user's goal of analyzing a dataset. Determining which of these candidate visualizations is most appropriate, however, remains challenging. Prior work has leveraged expert-curated taxonomies to guide visualization design and subsequent quality evaluation, a practical evaluation model must also account for human-centric factors. Latest visualization tools integrate Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate and refine visualizations, using LLM-as-a-judge to provide design feedback. Without a deeper understanding of whether, and in what ways, human and LLM perceptions of visualizations align, there is a real risk of deploying low-quality agents that do not reflect human judgment. We study this question through a pilot experiment - we formulate the problem as a preference task over curated chart pairs and compare the judgments of state-of-the-art vision models with those of a panel of human annotators. We establish a cautionary tale: such judges risk filtering out informative, compelling displays. We find that frontier models collapse human subjectivity, a rich signal that reveals contrasting design choices, into near-deterministic verdicts.

papers.title: Beyond Identity Creation: Bilinear Sybil Cost in Identities and Time
papers.summary: Sybil defenses price the creation of an identity, yet influence goes, again and again, to active identities. We study the cost of maintaining influence. A defense has a bilinear Sybil cost with ratio $A$ if keeping $s$ identities active for $T$ periods costs at least $sT/A$ honest units: the average cost per identity-window is at least $1/A$ times an honest participant's cost. Recurrence alone does not guarantee this cost. The cost can be carried over from earlier periods, shared among many identities, or be negligible when fast hardware does the work of thousands of honest devices. We give four sufficient conditions for a defense that checks every identity each period to achieve bilinear Sybil cost: identity binding, freshness, a shared deadline, and sequential, non-batchable work. They yield two guarantees: a bilinear total cost, with $A$ the speed advantage of the adversary's fastest hardware, and, because the work must be fresh and finished by a common deadline, a bound on the identities active in a period by the processors running at that time. We prove that none of the four follows from the other three. A verifiable delay function on an identity-bound input meets all four without payments, with $A$ of 2 to 8 for CPUs and about 28 for a hypothetical ASIC, against $10^3$ to $10^7$ for hash puzzles. We measure one active identity per core per period against about 80,000 under a signed heartbeat, no gain from batching up to 1,000 identities, and rejection of all tested attacks.
papers.comment: 16 pages, 4 figures. Main paper followed by the supplementary material. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

papers.title: Online Bayesian Inference for a Dirichlet Process Mixture of Binary Logit Models
papers.summary: Flexible travel behaviour models for preference heterogeneity have largely remained within the batch-estimation paradigm. The growing availability of continuously collected behavioural data, for example from smartphone applications, highlights the need for methods that update posterior inference on such heterogeneity as new observations arrive. This study proposes an online Bayesian inference method for a Dirichlet process mixture of binary logit models. The main challenge is to update the posterior as observations arrive while allowing the latent cluster structure to expand and historical cluster assignments to be revised. We develop a sequential Monte Carlo sampler using a sequence of Pólya--Gamma-augmented partial-data posteriors, local particle-weight corrections, and recursively maintained sufficient statistics. Each observation's contribution can be added, removed, or replaced in these summaries, supporting both sequential coefficient updating and rejuvenation that revisits historical cluster assignments. The simulation study shows that observation-by-observation sequential updating yields final posterior summaries close to those obtained by batch Markov chain Monte Carlo. Sensitivity analyses further demonstrate trade-offs between posterior approximation accuracy and computational cost as the number of particles and rejuvenation settings are varied. An illustrative empirical application shows how the method tracks posterior evolution and produces observation-specific provisional posterior summaries with low latency as real-world trip records are processed sequentially. The proposed approach provides a methodological foundation for online inference in travel behaviour models with parameter heterogeneity and for future extensions to richer choice structures, low-latency decision support, and online anomaly screening.

papers.title: Analysis of Local Open-Weight LLM Agents on Vulnerability-Reproduction Tasks
papers.summary: Open-weight language models that fit on a single consumer GPU are becoming capable on a growing range of tasks, and they matter because they can run locally without sending the code to a hosted service. Vulnerability reproduction, turning a vulnerability description into an input that crashes the vulnerable build, is a natural target for them, since it is an automated analysis task closer to test generation than to code comprehension and it runs against a build that must be executed rather than read. In order to assess whether current models can perform it, we evaluate twelve configurations of local models, spanning three generations, two architectures and three quantization levels, on ten CyberGym vulnerability-reproduction tasks, three runs each under one harness, and release the full artefact. We show that every configuration, down to the 4B model, solves most of the six easier tasks, and configurations separate only on the remaining four. For the harder tasks, the 27B model is required. Quantization did not change what the models solved in any matched pair, but it changed how fast they got there, and the mixture of experts reached the same scores in less wall clock. We also examine the agent trajectories. Almost every run we examined, including those that fail, names the vulnerable function and states the correct hypothesis, and what separates a solved task from an unsolved one is whether that hypothesis becomes a working input.
papers.comment: 35 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Preprint of a manuscript under review at the Journal of Systems and Software (Elsevier). Artefact: https://doi.org/10.57967/hf/10888

papers.title: Missing solutions in scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
papers.summary: We discover novel neutron star solutions under scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (sGB) gravity which have been missed altogether in the existing literature. The complete solution space also reveals a new regularity condition that has to be satisfied by all scalarized stars. Certain scalarized branches of neutron star solutions under sGB gravity have long been known to abruptly terminate on stellar mass-radius diagrams at lower stellar radii, a phenomenon that has no counterpart in classical scalar-tensor theories. Such termination has been strongly suspected to be physical rather than a numerical artifact nevertheless, since sGB theories feature a regularity condition at the center of the star, which can prevent the existence of certain configurations. Motivated by the recently re-emerging phase-transition view of scalarization, we first predict that these terminated branches can reappear after a "gap." We confirm this by finding such reappearing branches, and also determine which parts of the theory parameter space are more amenable to such occurrences. We then show that the previously known central regularity condition cannot explain all the non-existing solutions in the gaps, which leads us to the discovery of a new, non-central, condition for the existence of scalarized neutron stars under sGB gravity.

papers.title: Hyperbolic Nanocavities for Single-Molecule Vibrational Strong Coupling
papers.summary: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) in low-loss anisotropic materials such as hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) provide extreme sub-diffractional field confinement in the mid-infrared, making them attractive for enhancing the interaction of light with molecular vibrations. Collective vibrational strong coupling between molecular ensembles and HPhPs has already been demonstrated in extended slabs. Reaching this regime with a single molecule, however, remains a major challenge, and would provide a platform for investigating how vacuum electromagnetic fields influence molecular dynamics and chemical reactivity. Here, we show theoretically that single-molecule vibrational strong coupling can be reached in hBN nanocavities that laterally confine HPhPs within a finite volume. Combining full-wave electromagnetic simulations with the few-mode quantization approach, we find that these nanocavities support a rich set of asymmetric resonances that strongly enhance the local spectral density, with frequencies that follow from simple HPhP ray trajectories and can be tuned through the cavity aspect ratio. We identify resonances with quality factors of about $600$ and effective mode volumes of $|V_{\mathrm{eff}}| \sim 10^{-7}λ^{3}$, sufficient for single-molecule strong coupling with vibrational transitions with dipole moments on the order of $1\,\mathrm{D}$. These results establish hyperbolic nanocavities as a promising platform for single-molecule vibrational strong coupling and open new routes toward the local control of vibrational dynamics and molecular energy flow.

papers.title: Finite-time mixing and reaction in packed bed reactors
papers.summary: We investigate mixing dynamics in porous media at finite times, using pore-scale lattice-Boltzmann simulations combined with Lagrangian particle tracking. We compute fluid deformation in randomly packed beds based on the moving Protean frame approach introduced by Lester 2018. From the extracted Lagrangian kinematics, we construct a mixing model based on lamellar aggregation that well predicts the Eulerian scalar fields obtained from simulations. Our results reveal an early time mixing regime dominated by shear-driven fluid deformation, where solute mixing arises from the random overlap of diffusive concentration elements. In this regime, mixing proceeds slowly and follows a temporal decay of concentration variance, $σ_c^2 \sim Pe^{-α/(2α+1)} t^{-1/2}$, where Pe is the Peclet number and $α$ the exponent characterizing shear deformation. This dynamic arises when the Peclet number is small relative to the ratio between the exponential-mixing and shear-deformation timescales. This analysis also demonstrates that shear-induced mixing govern the homogenization of early-stage reactions at the fluid-solid interface in finite-size random packed beds, typically operating at moderate Peclet numbers $Pe =O(10^2)$.
papers.journal: Journal of Fluid Mechanics , Volume 1034 , 10 May 2026 , A9

papers.title: Understanding the Perception of Transliterated Offensive Social Media Posts Among Banglish and Hinglish Users
papers.summary: Effective content moderation depends on understanding not just what harmful content looks like, but how users perceive and respond to it. When offensive language is written in transliterated forms such as Banglish or Hinglish (Bangla or Hindi in Latin script), it may be interpreted very differently than in native scripts, with direct consequences for whether users report, ignore, or recognize it as harmful. Yet little is known about how script choice relates to user perception, or how these perceptions vary across demographic groups. To investigate these perceptions, we conducted a user study with $310$ participants ($193$ Hindi, $60$ Bangla, $57$ Bangla-Hindi bilingual speakers) who evaluated offensive posts in native scripts and transliterations. Participants provided offensiveness scores ($4.03$ for Banglish, $3.86$ for Hinglish) to transliterated posts, yet reporting fell from $20.9\%$ (native - Bangla, Hindi) to $18.2\%$ (transliterated - Banglish, Hinglish). Ignoring remained the dominant response (range $25.38\%-44\%$ overall). Women reported at higher probability than men for native-script ($23.6\%$ vs. $17.7\%$) and showed almost identical reporting probability in comparison to men for transliterated posts ($17.5\%$ vs. $17.9\%$), and younger participants ($<40$) rated Banglish content as more offensive than older participants ($\geq 40$), (Overall offensive score: $3.99$ vs. $3.78$). These findings identify transliteration as critical blind spot for moderation, underscoring the need for linguistically sensitive approaches to online safety.

papers.title: Explainable Anomaly Detection in 5G Networks through Continuous Time Graphs
papers.summary: 5G networks increasingly resemble distributed systems in their design. It then becomes crucial to move beyond traditional network-based detection methods and to explore alternative approaches. In this work, we propose a formalization of 5G network exchanges as a dynamic graph, on which we apply techniques from the field of graph-based learning to detect anomalies effectively. This representation allows for fine-grained analysis of packet-level semantic content, while simultaneously capturing sequential and topological contexts, both of which are essential for identifying sophisticated and multi-stage attacks. To assess the effectiveness of this formalism, we evaluate it with the most popular dynamic graph models, demonstrating its potential for 5G anomaly detection.
papers.journal: The International Conference on Future and Intelligent Communication and Networking, Dec 2026, San Antonio (Texas), United States

papers.title: Spatial structure of surface plasmon resonance under narrow-beam illumination and its implications for sensing
papers.summary: The reflection of light on a surface plasmon resonance structure can be understood as the interference between the direct Fresnel reflection and the light radiated back by the plasmon as it propagates along the metal film. When the beam waist is only an order of magnitude larger than the surface plasmon propagation length, these two contributions separate spatially, and their destructive interference localizes into a dark fringe within the reflected beam. We develop an analytical model of this effect, design a realistic setup based on off-the-shelf components to observe it, and simulate the complete experiment, from illumination to detection, with an open-source framework. In the regime where the interference is maximized, the spatial structure of the reflected beam becomes extremely sensitive to the outer medium. This allows us to define an observable more than an order of magnitude more sensitive than amplitude-based measurements, and we expect a comparable improvement in resolution.

papers.title: Riemannian Optimization-based Whole-body Obstacle Avoidance for Mobile Continuum Robots in Cluttered Environments
papers.summary: Inspired by the coordination of global motion and local shape adaptation in snakes, elephant trunks, and octopus arms, we propose a unified planning and control framework for mobile continuum robots in cluttered and confined environments. Existing approaches often address high-level path planning and local motion control separately, limiting coordinated base-arm motion, kinematic consistency, and collision avoidance. Our framework integrates long-horizon trajectory planning with real-time geometric refinement under kinematic and environmental constraints. The global layer combines A* search with minimum-jerk planning to generate smooth reference trajectories. The local layer uses a geometry-consistent inverse kinematics solver and Riemannian optimization to coordinate mobile-base motion and continuum deformation while avoiding obstacles. We evaluate the framework through simulated pipe-traversal tasks with multiple baseline planners and real-world experiments involving navigation among dense obstacles and manipulation in confined spaces. Results demonstrate improved motion consistency, feasibility, and adaptability, supporting coordinated whole-body motion of mobile continuum robots in constrained environments.

papers.title: CoSafe: Cooperative Runtime Safety Assurance for Mixed-Traffic Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: With the rapid development of autonomous driving systems (ADSes), real-world roads are evolving into mixed-traffic environments where autonomous vehicles (AVs) and other traffic participants (e.g., human-driven vehicles (HDVs), cyclists, and pedestrians) coexist and interact with each other. However, current ADSes still incur various safety violations in mixed traffic scenarios, raising a strong demand for runtime safety assurance frameworks that can continuously monitor hazards and prevent potential violations. Existing ego-centric assurance approaches are insufficient for mixed traffic, where violations often arise from locally reasonable yet jointly incompatible decisions among multiple vehicles and cannot be reliably resolved through independent takeover. To bridge this gap, we propose CoSafe, a modular and ADS-agnostic cooperative runtime safety assurance framework for mixed-traffic autonomous driving to extend runtime safety assurance from ego-centric takeover to scene-level cooperative intervention. CoSafe leverages vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication to enable roadside units (RSUs) to monitor scene-level hazards and jointly mitigate hazards involving multiple vehicles. We integrate CoSafe with seven state-of-the-art ADSes, and our evaluation on the InterDrive benchmark demonstrates that CoSafe improves the driving score of AVs by 70.03% on average, reduces safety violations by 87.80%, and accurately identifies unsafe AVs with an F3 score of 0.930, while satisfying real-time constraints.
papers.comment: Accepted by the 49th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE 2027). 13 pages

papers.title: Coupled membrane response and horizon dissipation in four-dimensional Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
papers.summary: We develop an action-based membrane paradigm for nonextremal, static, spherically symmetric black holes in four-dimensional Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (EsGB) gravity, describing their interaction with external perturbations through an effective fluid membrane. We calculate the linear membrane responses to perturbations and use them to analyze the work done on the membrane and the energy absorbed by the horizon. Horizon energy absorption receives contributions from geometric shear and scalar interactions. The scalar contribution includes both direct work on the membrane and work associated with the induced horizon expansion. We then establish a balance relation between the integrated horizon absorption and the second-order change in Wald entropy between stationary horizon cuts. Applying this framework to slow dynamics near a simple turning point, we obtain the leading exponential growth or decay rate of spherically symmetric scalar perturbations without fitting a dynamical damping coefficient.

papers.title: Beyond the Landing Page: Website Blocking, Tracker Visibility, and Human Alignment in Automated Web Crawls
papers.summary: Web tracking studies largely rely on automated crawlers, yet their measurements can differ from what people encounter while browsing. Conventional crawlers follow predefined navigation rules, whereas LLM-driven agents decide how to navigate and interact with websites, potentially changing the tracking they encounter. We compare agentic and non-agentic crawlers to examine how websites respond to them, what tracking they record, and how closely their observations match human browsing. Across 2,000 popular websites, we evaluate different navigation strategies, automation frameworks, and stealth configurations, alongside browsing data from 26 participants. We find that website denials increase beyond landing pages for standard browser automation, while a detection-resistant automation framework largely prevents this escalation without increasing recorded tracking. On the same URLs, agentic crawlers record tracking activity from 1.5-1.7 times as many third-party organizations, particularly on consent-managed pages. Agentic crawlers recover 82-87% of tracker organizations observed by participants, compared with 58-68% for non-agentic crawlers, yet roughly half of their own observations are absent from human participant visits. These findings show that avoiding website interventions, increasing tracking visibility, and achieving closer agreement with human observations do not necessarily go hand in hand, highlighting the need to select and validate crawlers according to the measurement objective.

papers.title: GPUMAP: GPU-Accelerated Progressive Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection
papers.summary: Dimensionality reduction (DR) techniques are fundamental to the analysis of high-dimensional data, yet their substantial computational cost limits their use in interactive settings. To address this limitation, we present GPU-accelerated Progressive Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (GPUMAP), an efficient progressive DR algorithm designed for interactive use. We identify three atomic operations within UMAP and restructure them into a progressive pipeline. As part of this adaptation, we introduce modifications to UMAP, including operation queues, instance-wise local join, and scheduling strategies. We further accelerate computation by leveraging GPU parallelism, enabling interactive analysis of million-scale datasets on commodity GPU hardware. Finally, we employ our implementation to systematically study the behavior of progressive DR, investigating how projections evolve over time relative to the ground-truth projection and how biased data streams influence the quality and stability of the resulting projections.

papers.title: A minimal E/I circuit model explains differential recovery from amblyopia under TTX and reverse occlusion
papers.summary: Recovery from amblyopia beyond the critical period remains a major challenge in visual neuroscience. Experimental studies show that transient inactivation of the fellow eye with tetrodotoxin (TTX) produces stronger and more persistent recovery than reverse occlusion (RO), despite both interventions reducing competition from the fellow eye. The circuit mechanisms underlying this difference remain unclear. We develop a minimal cortical circuit model combining excitatory-inhibitory population dynamics, BCM-like metaplasticity, homeostatic regulation, and eye-specific synaptic plasticity. Monocular deprivation drives the network into an amblyopic operating regime with reduced excitatory activity and fellow-eye dominance. Phase-plane and operating-regime analyses show that TTX and RO subsequently place the circuit in distinct dynamical states. TTX lowers inhibitory activity while maintaining excitatory activity above the BCM modification threshold, creating a larger plasticity-permissive regime than RO. These differences produce stronger recovery of amblyopic-eye responsiveness and greater correction of ocular dominance under TTX. A local robustness analysis across 300 perturbed parameter sets shows that the TTX advantage is not dependent on a narrowly tuned parameter choice. These results provide a mechanistic account of the differential efficacy of fellow-eye inactivation and suggest that recovery from sensory deprivation depends not only on changes in sensory input, but also on the dynamical operating regime of the cortical circuit.
papers.comment: 24 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to PLOS Computational Biology

papers.title: ProGram: A Grammar for Progressive Computation Pipelines
papers.summary: Progressive Visual Analytics (PVA) systems have demonstrated the effectiveness of time-bounded, incremental computation for exploring large-scale data. However, our survey reveals that existing PVA implementations are often difficult to reuse and extend, as their progressive behaviors are typically realized through ad hoc, hard-coded mechanisms distributed across servers and clients. To address this limitation, we present ProGram, a grammar for progressive computation pipelines. Informed by a comprehensive analysis of prior concepts and design practices in existing PVA systems, ProGram is designed to support core progressive features while reducing implementation burden. Furthermore, we extend the design space by introducing novel mechanisms, such as lockstepping, forking, and temporary prioritization, to better support diverse usage scenarios. Finally, we demonstrate the expressiveness and coverage of ProGram by reproducing and extending existing progressive visualization systems, presenting a gallery of progressive computation pipelines, and discussing the grammar coverage.

papers.title: FireOPS: A Human-Centric Emergency Operations Platform
papers.summary: Volunteer fire brigades rely on fragmented alerting channels and radio plus paper for situational awareness, hindering a shared common operational picture (COP). FireOPS integrates smartphone alerting, navigation, a live geospatial COP, a district resource-load overview and contextual manuals into a human-centric decision-support surface for commanders and responders, running on an edge + cloud architecture whose dual-channel provides source-level redundancy against failure of either the radio or the provincial server feed; delivery to smartphones still depends on the cloud core and mobile networks. This lessons-learned report presents the design rationale, positions FireOPS within emergency-response information systems research, and reports operational findings from a primary log extract of a major regional flood in 2024 and from the 2025 public app release. A feature-matrix comparison with DIVERA 24/7, blaulichtSMS and the LifeRescue prototype identifies COP, decision support and dual-ingestion redundancy as the main differentiators, and we map the operational gaps observed during the flood to concrete engineering responses, deployed or in active development.

papers.title: Network Intrusion Forensic Detection System with Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Digital Chain of Custody
papers.summary: Deploying an explainable intrusion detection model from a validated laboratory setting into a forensic workflow requires guarantees that benchmarks do not test: that the certified model is the exact artifact applied to a case, that heterogeneous evidence can be classified reliably, and that every step is verifiable. We present MODEXRE, a forensic pipeline that extends a previously validated synthetic-data-trained XGBoost classifier with SHAP explainability (arXiv:2607.00763) into a dual-mode architecture: a Laboratory mode, where models are trained and certified on public and synthetic data, and a Formal mode, where a frozen, hash-verified model performs inference on case evidence under a SHA-256 hash-chained chain of custody. Suricata alerts, CEF firewall logs and packet captures are normalized through OCSF. Four design decisions, each triggered by an observed failure, shaped the architecture: a timestamp leak that inflated Kitsune performance (F1-macro 0.984, 0.662 after correction); a feature-coverage gap that made the 78-feature reference model misclassify a real SSH alert; causal temporal flow aggregation, which raised Kitsune multiclass F1-macro from 0.394 to 0.932; and a certification defect, exposed only by a real packet capture, whereby the pipeline had always trained a binary classifier. After correction, the same capture went from 100% of events flagged as malicious to 87% classified as Normal, with the scanning host identified as Reconnaissance. The default four-class certified model reaches F1-macro = 0.9538 on CICIDS2017-derived evidence; the recertified 18-category model reaches 0.6214, reflecting the real multiclass task. Chain-of-custody verification, model integrity hashing and per-prediction SHAP explanations are reported as measured outcomes.
papers.comment: 25 pages, 8 figures, 5 tables. Companion paper to arXiv:2607.00763

papers.title: Fluctuations in Environmental Resource Availability Alter the Oscillatory Tragedy of the Commons
papers.summary: Environmental noise in real-world complex systems--including fluctuations in temperature, humidity, and related environmental conditions--inevitably modulates individual metabolic capacity and, consequently, the efficiency of public-resource utilization. Yet conventional evolutionary game models incorporating environmental feedback treat resource dynamics deterministically. Here, we incorporate stochastic fluctuations into a noise-corrected replicator-dynamics framework. Theoretical analysis and stochastic birth-death simulations yield a counterintuitive result: moderate environmental noise stabilizes, rather than destabilizes, the interior fixed point across diverse payoff landscapes, while suppressing or eliminating catastrophic oscillations. These findings reframe environmental variability not merely as a perturbation but as a mechanism that fosters strategy coexistence and sustainable resource use in complex social and ecological systems.

papers.title: KVGuard: A KV Cache Safety Checker for LLM Serving Systems
papers.summary: Modern LLM serving systems manage the KV cache through PagedAttention, a custom GPU allocator that partitions a single CUDA-allocated region into fixed-size physical blocks and maps each request to those blocks through a CPU-built block table. This block-based design exposes a previously unstudied class of memory safety bugs in the KV cache, including double-free, use-after-free, out-of-bounds access, uninitialized read, and permission violation, which silently corrupt outputs or break request isolation without ever crashing the system. Existing memory sanitizers cannot detect them, because they reason about CUDA-level addresses rather than KV cache blocks, requests, and block tables, and their redzone- and quarantine-based designs do not fit the scarce GPU memory budget of LLM serving. This paper presents KVGuard, the first systematic memory-safety abstraction for KV cache management in LLM serving systems. KVGuard maintains a compact shadow block for each physical KV block, recording per-request permission and per-entry initialization, and uses this metadata to perform five safety checks across the PagedAttention workflow, spanning CPU allocation, block table construction and translation, and GPU-side block table lookup and KV entry access. Each check fires at the boundary that introduced the violation, enabling early detection during development rather than reporting downstream output corruption many requests later. A prototype of KVGuard on vLLM and SGLang covers all 29 historical real-world KV cache safety bugs collected from the two systems' patch histories. KVGuard further found 8 previously unknown safety violations while reporting no false positives. It adds 3.0% and 7.4% geomean TPOT overhead on Qwen 2.5 14B on vLLM and SGLang and at most 0.11% of the KV cache in memory overhead, two orders of magnitude below NVIDIA Compute Sanitizer on the same workloads.

papers.title: Growing One's AI Tools: A Paradigm of Practice-Grown Tools
papers.summary: Professionals have long used software built for them by others. This article reports the growth of a professional computer-assisted interpreting (CAI) tool built by its own user, a conference interpreter without programming training. Drawing on an eight-week version-controlled record with telemetry from 133 logged sessions and over 20,000 recognized utterances, the article traces how real conference work drove the tool through 62 commits and six versions. The record shows capabilities deployed on the day their need appeared and one strategy change that cut median end-to-end delay by over a third within one afternoon. The article then proposes the paradigm of practice-grown tools, defined by the shift from using to growing, the co-evolution of tool and practice through breakdown and repair, bounded local computation, and an assessment corollary, and it formulates three propositions toward tool-inclusive assessment of practitioners, from tool-making literacy to a compute-standardized format for certifying what they and their tools achieve together.

papers.title: From lattice QCD thermodynamics to an effective quasiparticle description of gluonic matter at finite temperature
papers.summary: We develop a lattice-constrained quasiparticle description of pure SU(3) Yang--Mills matter at finite temperature. The temperature-dependent effective gluon quasiparticle mass is determined from the lattice entropy density over $0.70\leq T/T_c\leq5$. It is interpreted as an effective thermal parameter encoding medium modifications of gluonic excitations, rather than as a physical gluon mass. With this mass fixed, we reconstruct the background contribution required for thermodynamic consistency, using a single pressure-normalization condition. The resulting pressure, energy density, entropy density, interaction measure, and squared speed of sound are then compared with available lattice results. Near $T_c$, the rapid variation of the effective mass is accompanied by a pronounced maximum in the interaction measure at $T/T_c\simeq1.09$, a strong suppression of the squared speed of sound, and a maximum in the background contribution. These correlated features characterize the substantial departure from conformal behavior in the transition region. At higher temperatures, the interaction measure decreases and the squared speed of sound approaches the conformal limit. We also examine the energy-per-excitation ratio $E/n_g$, which has a minimum of approximately $964~\mathrm{MeV}$ at $T/T_c\simeq1.21$. This ratio provides a measure of the excitation scale within the quasiparticle description. Overall, our results show how lattice thermodynamics can be mapped onto an effective gluonic excitation spectrum while maintaining thermodynamic consistency.

papers.title: Exponential Seniority Weighting Chain-Ladder Reserving
papers.summary: We develop a tractable state-space version of the chain-ladder model. The state-space dynamics acts on the accident year axis which, in contrast to the classical chain-ladder model, makes accident years dependent. This state-space version yields an exponential seniority weighting in the chain-ladder factor estimation, and it admits an analytical likelihood representation that enables us to compute the seniority weighted chain-ladder reserves and their prediction uncertainty: the one-year uncertainty is available in closed form and the total uncertainty requires a Monte Carlo simulation from the fully tractable likelihood representation.

papers.title: A Post-Quantum Interactive Hashing Theorem
papers.summary: Interactive hashing, introduced by Ostrovsky, Venkatesan, and Yung [OVY93], is a building block in many cryptographic protocols, including perfectly hiding commitments from one-way permutations [NOVY92]. Its multi-output generalization is a key ingredient in constructions of statistical zero-knowledge arguments for NP and statistically hiding commitments from arbitrary one-way functions [NOV06,HR07]. In this note, we give a post-quantum security proof for this multi-output interactive hashing protocol with arbitrary relations.

papers.title: When Predictive Fit Misleads: Selecting Marketing Mix Models Using Experimental RoAS Benchmarks
papers.summary: Marketing Mix Models (MMMs) are used to estimate channel-level Return on Ad Spend (RoAS) and guide marketing investment, yet competing specifications are usually compared on predictive-fit metrics such as out-of-sample R-squared, MAPE, or RMSE. We show that predictive fit can diverge from recovery of the causal quantities that drive marketing decisions. In simulations with known RoAS, the best-fitting specification is often not the one that recovers RoAS most accurately; replicated studies show that this disagreement is systematic and persists under media-spend collinearity, noise, and a misspecified carryover shape. Selecting specifications against experimental RoAS benchmarks, even imprecise ones, improves RoAS recovery relative to fit-based selection, and a real-world application with experimental benchmarks shows the same pattern. We propose an applied workflow: calibrate MMM specifications against estimand-aligned experimental benchmarks when they exist, and otherwise report RoAS sensitivity across plausible specifications rather than relying on a single best-fitting model.

papers.title: SenTrojan: Revealing Analog Hardware Trojan Attacks on Sensors
papers.summary: Sensors bridge the physical and digital worlds, making their integrity critical to cyber-physical system security. Existing sensor attacks largely exploit unintended and sensor-specific physical vulnerabilities, limiting their generalizability and motivating a different threat model, i.e., whether an adversary can implant hidden attack surfaces into sensors before deployment. In this paper, we present SenTrojan, an analog hardware Trojan framework for sensors. SenTrojan embeds malicious functionality into analog signal circuitry commonly shared across diverse sensor architectures, and activates the hidden behavior through crafted external physical signals. Once activated, SenTrojan can induce sensor malfunctions ranging from permanent denial-of-service to static or dynamic spoofing. To achieve these effects under different architectural constraints, we introduce two complementary designs. The Logic-Rule-Driven (LRD) Trojan adds lightweight analog monitoring logic to detect trigger features such as frequency and amplitude, enabling reliable activation across various sensor types. The Physical-Effect-Driven (PED) Trojan targets sensors with exploitable native analog effects, e.g., nonlinearity and rectification, and realizes attacks with minimal component insertion. We evaluate SenTrojan on 14 sensors spanning 6 transduction principles and demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse real-world scenarios. Overall, SenTrojan achieves an average successful trigger rate above 95%, maintains over 97% similarity to benign behavior, incurs zero false-trigger rate for LRD designs, and introduces less than 5% average deviation in drift, noise floor, and response time. To our knowledge, this work is the first systematic study of analog sensor Trojans, broadening sensor security from unintended physical vulnerabilities to intentional supply-chain compromise.

papers.title: Topology change and the Gauss Bonnet term in causal set theory: the sign of the cosmological term and the axion decay constant
papers.summary: Causal set theory permits changes of spatial topology without the metric degeneracy that forbids them in continuum Lorentzian gravity. In four dimensions such changes enter the gravitational action only through the Gauss--Bonnet term, which is the Euler density. We show that the Euler density of a discrete space is exact, local and combinatorial: it sums to the Euler characteristic at any resolution and is supported on topological defects. The Gauss--Bonnet term of a causal set is therefore fixed rather than postulated. Because it is linear in the number of elements, which is the four-volume, it acts as a cosmological constant. Its coefficient follows without forming any functional derivative, so the known obstruction in the continuum does not arise. The everpresent cosmological constant of causal set theory assumes that the mean topological charge vanishes. We show that it does not. The species of opposite sign solves the field equations only if a positive cosmological constant is already present, and, being simply connected, it cannot carry the axion charge that supports the other species. Only one sign survives, and the sign of the cosmological term is derived rather than assumed. We recover the surviving transition from the causal order alone in every simulated sprinkling. The action of the corresponding axion wormhole then fixes the magnitude. The observed value requires an axion decay constant near the grand unification scale, and this result is insensitive to the one-loop prefactor and to the Gauss--Bonnet coupling.

papers.title: Optimality of Separate Selling with Finite-Support Values
papers.summary: We characterize when separate selling is exactly revenue-optimal in multi-item auctions with additive buyers and independent, finitely supported valuations. For each item, the valuation distribution is identical across buyers, but it may differ across items. We show that, provided at least two items have a strictly positive non-top support value, separate selling is optimal for any number of buyers $n \ge 2$ if and only if top selling, which sells each item only at its highest possible value, is optimal for a single buyer. This equivalence holds under both dominant-strategy incentive compatibility and Bayesian incentive compatibility. We then characterize the optimality of top selling in the one-buyer problem through the existence of a particular class of dual flows and derive a necessary condition and several sufficient conditions on the value distributions for its optimality. These conditions reveal a common economic feature, which we call top-value isolation: high non-top valuations must be sufficiently far below the highest value or carry sufficiently little probability mass relative to the probability mass at the highest value.

papers.title: Reconciling Privacy with Provenance for Language Model Watermarks
papers.summary: Watermarking has great potential for regulating the use of language models (LMs), but its deployment has been marred by controversy, as many users argue that fine-grained tracking of LM usage violates their privacy. This tension reduces the effectiveness of watermarks, as users engage in evasion strategies such as paraphrasing that can remove much of the watermark signal. We show that provenance and privacy can be reconciled if we shift the goal of watermark design from tracking individuals to estimating aggregate usage. We develop locally differentially private watermarks which provably limit the evidence that any individual text can contribute to detection, while still enabling accurate estimation of population frequencies. We introduce the Red-Green Sequence (RGS) watermark, a private and computationally efficient watermark that achieves accurate frequency estimation at high privacy levels across various models, sample sizes and generation entropies in settings that reflect realistic deployment scenarios. On C4 language modeling tasks, we attain $0.0019$ MSE with $0.0038$ mean absolute bias at a low $\varepsilon$ of 1, while in more challenging settings such as an essay writing task with only 100 text samples, we still find errors on the order of $0.0113$ MSE with $0.004$ mean absolute bias at $\varepsilon=2$.

papers.title: Catastrophic Overfitting is Weight Drift the Training Loss Cannot See
papers.summary: Fast adversarial training (FAT) makes robust training affordable by replacing the multi-step attack with a single-step one, but it suffers from catastrophic overfitting (CO): partway through training, robustness to multi-step attacks collapses to near zero while the single-step attack used for training keeps being repelled. We show that CO is a quiet escape of the weights. Across the event the network's clean behavior quietly improves, and moving from the weights just before CO to those just after it changes the training objective only marginally while destroying most of the robustness. The training objective is therefore nearly blind to the displacement it causes, so it exerts no force to undo it. The exponential moving average (EMA) of the weights, which FAT protocols already maintain, does not accumulate this drift and stays robust through the entire event. This observation suggests a nearly free fix: when validation robustness drops, reset the weights to their EMA. We build this guard on top of a coupling-based base method designed so that its average stays inside the robust region. The resulting training removes CO in every one of our runs and attains the strongest AutoAttack accuracy among fast methods on all three benchmark datasets, including a clear margin on CIFAR-100, where it also clears the multi-step reference at roughly half its cost. Code is available at https://github.com/fzjcdt/co-weight-drift.
papers.comment: 12 pages (including appendix), 7 figures, 6 tables. Code available at https://github.com/fzjcdt/co-weight-drift

papers.title: Fluidic Body: Swarm Robots as a Fluid Extension of the Hand
papers.summary: Swarm robots have attracted growing interest as a physical interface for human--computer interaction, since a swarm can reshape its formation to fit the objects and surroundings it works with. For a human operator, however, adapting the swarm's behavior remains difficult. Most existing methods require the user to specify where the swarm should go, and they offer no intuitive way to change the collective's behavior as each task demands. We present Fluidic Body, a system that lets a person operate a swarm of fluid-imitating robots as an extension of the hand. The system places a virtual fluid between the hand and the swarm, and the user adapts the swarm's behavior to each task by changing the fluid's properties through simple hand movements. When the user opens the hand, the swarm becomes soft enough to deform and flow around obstacles. Closing the hand turns it into a hard, cohesive body that can push objects. We evaluated the controller's performance and its operability in two simulation experiments and one demonstration with physical robots. First, our controller handled both obstacle avoidance and object transportation better than an existing method that behaves the same way in every task. Second, in a VR user study, 17 participants completed the combined avoidance-and-transportation task faster and more reliably than with that method. They also reported a lower workload and a stronger sense of agency. Finally, this experience carried over to physical robots in a real-world demonstration (88 participants). These results suggest that treating a swarm as a fluid, a material people already understand, allows a robot swarm to work as a deformable extension of the human body.
papers.comment: accepted to ACM ISS 2026 (ISS track of PACMHCI)

papers.title: Offline Learning of Reserve Prices from Censored Bids
papers.summary: We study how a seller can learn a reserve price for a second-price auction from censored historical bid data. Because values below past reserves are unobserved, even unlimited data may not reveal which reserve earns the most revenue. Under a monotone hazard rate (MHR) assumption, we characterize exactly when an optimal reserve is identified, even though the value distribution may not be: either revenue has not yet begun to fall at the lowest historical reserve, so the best reserve lies among the observed bids, or the censored fraction is as large as MHR allows, which pins down the entire distribution. When identification fails, we derive the reserve that minimizes worst-case revenue regret over distributions consistent with the data, and prove that this unique minimax reserve and its regret depend on just two observable quantities: the censored fraction and the hazard just above the lowest historical reserve. With $N$ historical bidders, the optimal reserve is learned with expected worst-case regret $O(N^{-1/2})$ when it lies among the observed bids, and $O(N^{-1})$ from the censored count alone when the censored fraction is as large as MHR allows and the optimum lies at or below the lowest reserve. In the nonidentifiable regime, plugging estimates of the two quantities into the minimax reserve gives expected worst-case regret within $O(N^{-2/5})$ of the population minimum under local density smoothness, with a matching minimax lower bound on a smooth class. Beyond MHR, we solve the minimax problem for regular and unrestricted distributions and prove an $O(N^{-2/5})$ learning bound in the regular nonidentifiable regime, given known bounds on the boundary parameters. Experiments on synthetic and eBay data show gains from exploiting MHR and the benefits of the robust rule when parametric models are misspecified.
papers.comment: 87 pages, 12 figures, 25 tables. Authors listed alphabetically

papers.title: Securing Web Agents with the Compile-Then-Execute Paradigm
papers.summary: Web agents commonly follow the ReAct paradigm, selecting each action from runtime observations that inherently mix trusted and untrusted content. This design makes their control flow vulnerable to prompt injections embedded in webpages. We introduce Baya, a compile-then-execute web agent designed to prevent prompt-injection-driven control-flow hijacking by design. Before accessing the live website, Baya compiles the user's request into an executable Python program that calls a Trusted Website API. The planning model does not observe live website content; only the compiled program processes it. Untrusted data may determine program values or select among branches defined during compilation, but it cannot redefine the user task or cause the model to synthesize new website operations at runtime. The Trusted Website API gives the compiler a unified view of the website's action space, enabling ahead-of-time planning without the stepwise action discovery required by reactive agents. Our evaluation across 581 valid WebArena Verified tasks shows that Baya achieves 77.8% aggregate utility, outperforming browser-only ReAct (55.1%) and API-enabled ReAct (66.7%). On WASP, a security benchmark for web agents, Baya achieves 0% attack success rate, compared with 16.2% for API-enabled ReAct and 25.5% for browser-only ReAct.

papers.title: PIMROP: A Feasibility Study of Return-Oriented Programming on Commercial Processing-in-Memory Architectures
papers.summary: Processing-in-Memory places small programmable cores on the memory device, where they execute beside the DRAM banks and beyond the control-flow defenses that protect host programs. The security of this in-memory code is an attack surface that remains largely unstudied. We present PIMROP, to our knowledge the first demonstrated code-reuse attack on a commercial Processing in-Memory ISA. We show that return-oriented programming is feasible on a real, commercially shipped PIM instruction set, the UPMEM DPU, whose DRAM Processing Units run C compiled by a dedicated LLVM toolchain. We build Galileo-for-DPU, a gadget scanner adapted to the DPU's fixed-width, 8-byte-aligned RISC encoding, and run it entirely on the UPMEM functional simulator in a reproducible Docker and VM environment. We find the runtime library that every kernel links already yields 517 non-trivial gadgets covering all five canonical ROP primitive classes, and all 13 PrIM benchmarks we scanned carry gadgets as well. We then demonstrate two verified end-to-end attacks, each reproducible on 10 of 10 runs. In the first, a stack buffer overflow in a DPU kernel overwrites the saved return address and diverts control into a routine that copies a secret into host-readable memory. In the second, we leak the same secret using a chain of reused gadgets alone, without diverting control into any such routine. We further show that two standard defenses--stack canaries and _FORTIFY_SOURCE-style bounds-check fortification--fail on the DPU in ways specific to the platform (misplaced canary, silently inactive wrapper), and we verify a bounds-checked DMA that stops the attack on 10 of 10 runs with no effect on benign requests. To enable further research on PIM security, we open-source Galileo-for-DPU and our testing harness at https://github.com/wtegge2/ROP-in-PIM.

papers.title: CoordX Protocol: Peer to Peer Cryptographically Verified Shared Records
papers.summary: People, companies and software agents often must work on shared records even when they do not trust each other. Today they usually give those records to a central server. The server keeps the canonical copy, authenticates users, and decides who has permissions to act on the record. The CoordX Protocol removes the need for that central server. In the CoordX protocol the author of a record holds full permission over it. Permission for any other party to create, read or update the record is assigned by explicit grants and keys. An invitation only starts contact between two parties. It gives no permission. Each record is a causal tree of signed entries, and each entry is immutable. Each entry names the permission that allowed it. Any party can get the proof of that permission and check it without help from anyone. Two honest parties that check the same bytes, with the same keys and local settings, always get the same answer. The content is encrypted, so the relays that may carry it in transit see only sealed bytes. To exclude a party from future content, the other parties move to new keys. The protocol does not choose a winning version, does not put entries in time order, and does not need global agreement. Applications decide what the entries mean above the level of the protocol.

papers.title: Can a self-sustaining chemical network emerge due to just a few catalysts?
papers.summary: Understanding how self-sustaining chemical reaction networks can emerge from simple molecules is an important question in chemical approaches to the origin of life. Reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated (RAF) sets provide a mathematical framework for investigating this question. This line of research goes back to the early work of Kauffman on autocatalytic reaction networks and was subsequently developed through the probabilistic framework of Mossel and Steel. Further contributions by Hordijk, Steel, and collaborators extended the theory to more heterogeneous forms of catalysis, including reaction-dependent probabilities or power-law distributions of catalytic activity. We introduce a stochastic model that combines heterogeneous molecular catalytic activity with reaction-dependent molecule-reaction compatibility. By assigning random catalytic weights to molecules and incorporating compatibility through an explicit formulation of catalysis probabilities, our model provides a concrete and flexible setting that captures both sources of heterogeneity while remaining mathematically tractable. We establish novel and general criteria for RAF formation and nonformation. We further demonstrate that classical phase-transition criteria need not remain valid in the presence of reaction-dependent catalysis. For heavy-tailed catalytic weights, we identify and rigorously quantify an additional phase transition. In models with finite-mean catalytic weights, RAF formation and nonformation are governed by a catalytic intensity parameter. For infinite-mean weights, however, we show that RAFs may emerge with probability tending to one even when the catalytic intensity parameter tends to zero.

papers.title: Who Pays for the Knowledge Models Copy? Model Collapse as Rogers' Paradox
papers.summary: Generative models trained on the output of earlier models lose knowledge across generations, rare knowledge first. The remedies that work all bring in information from outside the loop, and the theory of model collapse treats that supply as given: a fixed archive, drawn from a fixed distribution. We argue that the supply is the problem, and that cultural evolution has the theory of it. We read model collapse as Rogers' paradox: a population that comes to rely on copying ends up no better off than one that never copied, because copies go stale unless someone keeps learning for themselves. We test the identification in three steps. First, Rogers' model, fitted only to fully synthetic training, predicts to within a few percentage points how much rare knowledge language models, from word trigrams to a pretrained transformer, retain under other mixtures of fresh data. Second, when the world itself changes, a lineage that copies its own past needs more fresh data to keep up the faster the world changes, as Rogers' model says it must and as analyses that assume a fixed target cannot; a lineage that restarts every generation from fixed pretrained weights is largely insulated, because those weights are knowledge that is never copied. Third, we close the loop: when the people who write a model's training data can ask the model instead of finding things out, the supply of fresh data becomes endogenous. At equilibrium, the model is exactly as reliable as it is costly for people to find out for themselves, the population is no better off than without the model, and every increase in the share of model-written text must be paid for by more people learning for themselves. Users who check what they are told and relearn when it is wrong break the paradox. Filters that select plausible text are conformist and accelerate collapse; only checks that carry new information act as critical learning.

papers.title: Research on gravitational waves from extreme mass ratio inspirals in an axisymmetric Finslerian extension of Schwarzschild spacetime
papers.summary: We investigate gravitational waves from extreme mass ratio inspirals in an axisymmetric Finslerian extension of the Schwarzschild spacetime. Its angular component is described by a two-dimensional Randers space, with the Schwarzschild limit recovered at Finslerian parameter $ε= 0$. This structure breaks spherical symmetry, causing generic orbits to undergo orbital plane precession. Using multipolar radiation reaction and adiabatic orbital averaging, we derive the leading order Finslerian corrections to the energy, axial angular momentum, and total angular momentum fluxes. These corrections enter at Newtonian order and take different forms. We then incorporate these corrections into a higher-order Schwarzschild hybrid flux model to evolve the orbital elements and construct waveforms at mass quadrupole order using the numerical kludge method. The Finslerian corrections affect both the conservative orbital dynamics and the dissipative inspiral, producing cumulative phase shifts relative to the Schwarzschild waveform. For the representative source observed by LISA over one year with signal-to-noise ratio of 20, the noise weighted mismatch analysis shows that Finslerian waveforms with $|ε| \gtrsim 2 \times 10^{-6}$ are distinguishable from their Schwarzschild counterparts, with higher initial eccentricities further lowering the distinguishable value of $|ε|$. For a Schwarzschild injection, the Fisher matrix analysis yields a marginalized $1σ$ uncertainty of $σ_ε\simeq 1.26 \times 10^{-6}$. These results show the potential of space-based gravitational wave detectors to probe the axisymmetric Finslerian extension of the Schwarzschild spacetime.

papers.title: Time-Varying Tails: Estimation, Inference, and Risk Measurement
papers.summary: Motivated by evidence that the tails of economic and financial time series need not be stable over time, we develop a framework for studying time-varying tails. We model the extreme value index as a smooth function of time in the locally stationary framework of Zhou and Wu (2009). We estimate it by a ratio-form kernel Hill estimator in which a single intermediate quantile thresholds the whole local window. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality, and we construct uniform confi- dence bands. We also propose a consistent test of tail stability under extremal clustering. Combined with the Weissman extrapolation method, the estimator of the extreme value index yields time- varying extreme Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall. In an empirical application, we find the tail of daily loss of S&P 500 is compatible with a constant shape, whereas that of volatility-filtered loss varies significantly.

papers.title: Spacetime Evolution Induced by a Massive Cosmic String in Numerical Relativity
papers.summary: Cosmic strings are one-dimensional topological defects formed during phase transitions in the early universe. ''Massive'' cosmic strings possess a sufficiently large tension to close their transverse space, forming a conical singularity outside the string, as a static gravitational effect. In a dynamical context, such strings are expected to drive topological inflation. In this work, we investigate the spacetime evolution induced by the formation of a massive cosmic string in a radiation-dominated cosmological background, imposing cylindrical symmetry. Using full numerical relativity simulations, we observe that the string core undergoes topological inflation and that its boundary moves inwards superluminally, which causally disconnects the core from the outer universe. Between the core and the asymptotic regions, a nearly matter-dominated decelerating region originates sourced by the oscillating string fields. This region is bounded by a local maximum (''belly'') and local minimum (''throat'') of the circumferential radius, while the throat recedes outwards at about 10% the speed of light. Furthermore, a gravitational wavefront is emitted from the string, characterizing the light cone of the string formation. Even behind the wavefront, the exterior region no longer exhibits a ''conical'' structure. Based on the simulation results, we construct a Penrose diagram, reflecting the causal structure of the entire spacetime.

papers.title: Quantum Key Exchange from Public Quantum Money
papers.summary: Two-message quantum key exchange (2QKE) cannot be realized in a statistically secure way, and therefore some computational assumptions are required.
